subject: chemistry
title: Flame tests
key_idea: (Separate science) A flame test identifies some metal ions from the colour they give a flame. Lithium is crimson, sodium yellow, potassium lilac, calcium orange-red and copper green. A mixture of ions can mask some colours.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers the flame colour of each metal ion you need to know.

items.meaning: A test that identifies some metal ions (cations) from the colour they give a Bunsen flame.

diagram.alt: Pick a metal ion to see its flame colour.

items: Five ions to know: lithium, sodium, potassium, calcium and copper.
Flame colours of other metal ions are not required.

sections.heading: How to do a flame test

blocks.text: This section covers the method and why each step matters.

diagram.alt: Put the steps of a flame test in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps of a flame test in order
steps: Clean the wire with hydrochloric acid, then hold it in a roaring flame until the flame is colourless
Dip the clean wire into the sample
Hold the wire in the hottest part of a blue Bunsen flame
Observe and record the flame colour

items: Clean the wire between samples, so earlier samples do not contaminate the colour.
Wet the wire, for example with acid, so the solid sticks and vaporises more easily.
Hold the sample in the hottest part of the flame, the tip of the blue cone, for a bright colour.
A wooden splint can be used instead of a wire, but it can burn and change the flame colour.
Clean wire, sample on the wire, blue flame, note the colour.

blocks.text: This section covers why a flame test can be hard to read.

items: If a sample contains a mixture of ions, some flame colours can be **masked**.
A flame test identifies metal ions (cations), not the negative ions.
A flame test on a dirty wire shows a blend of colours.
A mixture of ions can mask flame colours.
A flame test shows the metal ion only.

checks.q: Name the metal ion that gives a lilac flame.
Why must the wire be cleaned between flame tests?
checks.a: Otherwise the previous sample is still on the wire, so the colours mix (are masked).

checks.q: Describe how to do a flame test using a metal wire and a Bunsen burner.
checks.a: Put the sample on a (clean) wire. Hold the wire in the blue (non-luminous) flame and observe the flame colour.

worked_example.question:
Lithium carbonate is used in medicines and contains lithium ions and carbonate ions.

A student tested a tablet for lithium ions and for carbonate ions using:
a metal wire
dilute hydrochloric acid
limewater.

Plan an investigation to show the presence of lithium ions and of carbonate ions in the tablet.

You should include the results of the tests for the ions.
answer_points: Lithium: crush the tablet, or dissolve it in water or acid.
Clean the wire, place the tablet sample on the wire and put it in a blue (roaring, non-luminous) flame.
Observe the flame colour: a crimson flame shows lithium ions.
Carbonate: add dilute hydrochloric acid to the tablet and see the fizzing (effervescence).
Bubble the gas through limewater: the limewater turns cloudy, which shows carbonate ions.
worked_example.tip: A levelled question: give both tests, in a clear order, with both results.

worked_example.question:
The table shows the results of flame tests on three compounds, P, Q and R.

Compound | Flame colour
P | red
Q | lilac
R | blue-green

Use the table to identify the metal ions in compounds P, Q and R.
answer_points: P: lithium (Li⁺). Strontium is also allowed.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each ion. Charges are ignored, even if incorrect.

worked_example.question:
Chemical tests are used to identify gases, anions and cations.

Fahmida uses the flame test to identify the cations in a solid.

Describe how Fahmida should do a flame test.
answer_points: Use a flame test wire (a wooden splint is also allowed).
Moisten the wire and dip it into the sample.
Introduce the sample into the blue flame of a Bunsen burner.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each stage: wire, moisten and dip, blue flame.

worked_example.question: Describe how to carry out a flame test.
answer_points: Use a wire or a splint to put the sample into a flame (M1)
Put the sample into a roaring (blue, hot) Bunsen flame and observe the colour (M2)

blocks.text: One more metal ion is needed, and two colours have other names.

items: Use a roaring (non-luminous) blue flame. A yellow safety flame is cooler and its own colour hides the colour of the sample.
Clean the wire between samples so that an earlier sample does not change the colour.

worked_example.question:
This question is about lithium and some of its compounds.

An unlabelled bottle containing a white powder is found in a laboratory.

Describe tests to show that the white powder in the bottle is lithium carbonate.
worked_example.tip: The flame test shows the lithium ion. The acid and limewater show the carbonate ion.

blocks.text: The colour names for two ions differ slightly.

items: Lithium ions give a red flame. Crimson is also correct.
Copper(II) ions give a blue-green flame. Green is also correct.
